meta.about: A whole-node rewrite (`target` + `text`, no `find`) on a bullet with inline markup. `setText` used to write only the LONGEST text run and leave the others exactly as authored, so the old bolded/emphasised word survived next to the new wording with no separating space. Fixed by rewriting every run: the new text goes to the run least likely to carry unwanted styling, the rest are blanked.
meta.recorded-outcome: Asked to replace the first bullet ('Orama for the client-side vector store', italicised on 'Orama') with all-new wording, the model reached for `find` with the bullet's whole current text — which spans the italic span and the plain run, so `replaceText` refused it as "spans several separately-styled pieces of text". That refusal named no way to replace a WHOLE node, only "try a single word", so the model spent the rest of the conversation alternating between narrower `find` phrases and an ambiguous `target: "the bullets"` guess, and one turn it repeated the plain-bullet 15.3 case (`A web-sized embedding model, quantized down`) and gave up without even calling the tool. Reproducing `edit_text({target: "15.3", text: ...})` directly (bypassing the model) showed the deeper bug: the whole-node path silently 'succeeded', but left "A web-sized embedding model" untouched and appended the new text straight after it with no space, because `mainRunIndex` picked the LONGEST run (", quantized down") to overwrite and left the rest alone.
meta.guards: two things, either alone reintroduces the bug. (1) `setText` in `chat/edit/apply.js`: writing only to `mainTextValue(el)`'s run and leaving the rest as authored, instead of blanking every other run in the same `pushAll` group — revert that and the `bullet 1: my friends call...` slide assertion below fails because the italic "Orama" survives. (2) The spanning-refusal message in `replaceText`: drop the `target: "${spanning}" and no find` clause and the `asked` assertion on turn 1 fails.
